name: Grade
what: The designation of the stainless steel. Picking one fills in f_y, f_u and the family from the table.
why: Grade, f_y and f_u are linked: the table gives f_y and f_u for each grade, and the family sets the coefficients of Table B.1.
where: Table 5.1, by grade and product form. If your steel is not listed, choose Custom and enter f_y and f_u yourself.

name: Yield strength f_y
what: The 0.2 % proof strength: the stress where the steel starts to yield.
why: It sets the yield strain f_y / E and measures every slenderness in the method. Used in B.4, B.5, B.8 and B.13.
where: Table 5.1 by grade and product form, or the specified value. For cold-formed sections the averages f_ya and f_ua of 5.1.2.3 may be used (B.3(3)).

name: Ultimate tensile strength f_u
what: The highest stress the steel reaches in a tension test.
why: It fixes the top of the stress-strain curve of the CSM material model. Used in B.4 and B.5.
where: Table 5.1 by grade and product form, or the specified value. For cold-formed sections the averages f_ya and f_ua of 5.1.2.3 may be used (B.3(3)).

name: Family
what: The stainless steel family: austenitic, duplex or ferritic.
why: Each family has its own coefficients C₁, C₂ and C₃, which shape the CSM stress-strain curve and its strain limit.
where: Table B.1 lists the coefficients by family. A grade picked from Table 5.1 sets the family for you; for Custom, choose the family of your steel.

name: Modulus of elasticity E
what: Young's modulus: the stiffness of the steel in the elastic range.
why: It gives the yield strain f_y / E and appears in the plate and tube buckling stresses. Used in B.4, B.9 and B.11.
where: 5.1.5 gives E = 200 000 N/mm².

name: Values enhanced by cold-forming
what: Tick this if f_y and f_u are the averaged values of a cold-formed section, which include the strength gained by cold work.
why: B.3(3) allows the CSM to use these enhanced values for cold-formed sections.
where: Work out f_ya and f_ua as in 5.1.2.3 and enter them as f_y and f_u. Leave this unticked for the values of Table 5.1.

name: Section type
what: The shape of the cross-section.
why: B.2 lists the six shapes Annex B covers. The shape also decides which dimensions are asked and whether B.5 treats the section as flat plates or as a tube.
where: Your drawings or the manufacturer's section table. Choose one of the six shapes: I-section, channel, T-section, angle, rectangular hollow section or circular hollow section.

name: Fabrication
what: How the corner between web and flange is made: rolled, with a root radius r, or welded, with a weld leg s.
why: It decides whether you enter r or s, and both change the flat width c of the web and flange (8.2.2(5), Tables 7.2 and 7.3).
where: The manufacturer's data or your drawings.

name: Overall height h
what: The overall height of the section. For an angle, the length of the longer leg.
why: It gives the flat widths c of the plates (8.2.2(5)), which B.9 turns into the plate slenderness. It also drives the drawing and the section properties.
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings. The standard gives no values.

name: Overall width b
what: The overall width of the section. For an angle, the length of the shorter leg.
why: It gives the flat widths c of the flanges (8.2.2(5)), which B.9 turns into the plate slenderness. It also drives the drawing and the section properties.
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings. The standard gives no values.

name: Web thickness t_w
what: The thickness of the web, the plate that joins the flanges.
why: It shortens the flat widths c of the flange and web (8.2.2(5)) and sets the web slenderness in B.9.
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings. The standard gives no values.

name: Flange thickness t_f
what: The thickness of the flange.
why: It shortens the flat width c of the web (8.2.2(5)) and sets the flange slenderness in B.9.
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings. The standard gives no values.

name: Wall thickness t
what: The wall thickness of a hollow section, or the thickness of an angle leg.
why: It gives c = h − 3t for a rectangular hollow section (8.2.2(5)) and sets the slenderness in B.9 and B.11.
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings. The standard gives no values.

name: Root radius r
what: The radius of the rounded inside corner of a rolled section, between web and flange or at the heel of an angle.
why: In a rolled I-section, channel or T-section it shortens the flat widths c (8.2.2(5), Tables 7.2, 7.3). For an angle it changes only the section properties and the drawing.
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings.

name: Weld leg s
what: The leg length of the fillet weld that joins the web to the flange of a welded section.
why: It shortens the flat widths c of the web and flange (8.2.2(5), Tables 7.2 and 7.3).
where: Your fabrication drawings.

name: Outer corner radius r_o
what: The outside radius of the rounded corners of a rectangular hollow section. Enter 0 for sharp corners.
why: It changes only the section properties and the drawing. It does not change c = h − 3t (8.2.2(5)).
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings.

name: Outer diameter d
what: The outside diameter of a circular hollow section.
why: It gives the tube slenderness in B.10 and B.11.
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings. The standard gives no values.

name: Stem flat width c_stem
what: The flat width of the stem of a T-section: the straight part of the stem, clear of the corner.
why: B.9 needs a flat width for every plate. You type this one because the PDF draws no flat width for a T-section stem.
where: Measure it on your drawings.

name: Area A
what: The gross cross-sectional area of the member.
why: It turns stress into force in B.12, B.15 and B.16.
where: The manufacturer's section table, or the Use button in the Section geometry window, which copies the area computed from your dimensions.

name: Partial factor γM0
what: The partial safety factor applied to the resistance of the cross-section.
why: It divides the CSM resistance in B.12, B.15 and B.16, so a larger value gives a lower design resistance.
where: 8.1 NOTE gives 1.10 unless the National Annex gives another value.

name: Section has holes
what: Tick this if the section has bolt holes or slots.
why: The CSM tension route of B.6.1 does not cover sections with holes, so the tool stops and says why.
where: B.6.1(2) sends sections with holes to EN 1993-1-3:2024, 8.1.2 or EN 1993-1-1:2022, 8.2.3.

name: Slenderness from
what: How the slenderness of the section is found: from its dimensions, from flat plates entered one by one, or from a critical stress you type.
why: B.5 needs the critical buckling stress. Dimensions and plates use the plate formula B.9, a circular tube uses B.10 and B.11, and a typed σ_cr,cs skips them.
where: Choose the route that matches the data you have.

name: Poisson's ratio ν
what: How much a plate or wall shrinks sideways when it is stretched along its length.
why: It enters the plate and tube buckling stresses through 1 − ν². Used in B.9 and B.11. It is not used if you type σ_cr,cs.

name: Plastic strain limit Ω
what: A limit on the plastic strain you accept in the section, written as a multiple of the yield strain ε_y.
why: B.6 and B.7 cap the strain ratio at min(Ω, C₁ε_u/ε_y), so a smaller Ω gives a more conservative result.
where: 7.4.3.5 describes it as a project-specific limit on plastic strain. The PDF gives no value, so take it from the requirements of your project.

name: Critical stress σ_cr,cs
what: The elastic critical local buckling stress of the whole cross-section.
why: B.8 turns it into the slenderness that B.5 uses, and B.10 does the same for a tube. Typing it replaces the plate calculation of B.9.
where: B.5.2(2): numerical methods (for example a finite strip program) or the analytical expressions of reference [9]. Both are outside EN 1993-1-4.

name: Plate buckling factor k_σ
what: A number that says how well the edges of a plate are held and how the stress varies across it. A higher value means the plate buckles later.
why: B.9 uses it to find the critical buckling stress of the plate.
where: EN 1993-1-5:2024, 6.4.1, by plate support (internal plate or outstand) and stress ratio ψ. It is outside EN 1993-1-4.

name: Flat width b̄
what: The flat width of one plate: the straight part between the corners or welds, not the overall width.
why: B.9 uses it squared in the plate buckling stress, so it has a strong effect on the result.
where: Measure it on your drawings. For the six standard shapes, the Section dimensions route works it out by 8.2.2(5).

name: Plate thickness t
what: The thickness of this plate.
why: B.9 uses it in the plate buckling stress, together with the flat width.
where: The manufacturer's section table or the drawings.
